constructs.name: affective_state
constructs.description: Overall depressive/affective severity integrating mood, anhedonia, energy, and concentration. The latent target of the patient's question.

constructs.name: serotonergic_exposure
constructs.description: Effective pharmacological 5-HT reuptake inhibition at the synapse, driven by prescription dose, adherence, and individual pharmacokinetics. Decays with first-order kinetics; reaches steady state within ~7 days of a dose change.

constructs.name: adherence
constructs.description: Daily medication-taking behavior — whether the patient ingests the prescribed dose on a given day. Endogenous because depression severity itself reduces adherence.

constructs.name: sleep_quality
constructs.description: Sleep continuity and architecture (total duration, efficiency, REM%, sleep onset latency). Both a mediator of treatment effect and a reverse-caused outcome of mood.

constructs.name: physical_activity
constructs.description: Volume and intensity of physical movement (steps, exercise minutes, walking speed). Mediates a portion of treatment effect and reflects psychomotor state.

constructs.name: social_engagement
constructs.description: Frequency and density of interpersonal contact via messaging, calls, and in-person meetings. Behavioral activation through social contact.

constructs.name: prescription_event
constructs.description: Clinician-mediated prescribing and dispensing actions (initial prescription, dose changes, refills, formulary switches). Endogenous because initiation and dose escalation are partly responses to lagged symptom severity and follow-up assessments, while fills still drive subsequent exposure.

constructs.name: seasonal_load
constructs.description: Photoperiod-driven seasonal variation in mood baseline. Trough in mid-winter, peak in summer at Brooklyn latitude (40.7°N). Subclinical SAD spectrum.

constructs.name: life_events_load
constructs.description: Acute psychosocial stressor exposure: bereavement, relationship loss, financial shocks, family illness, geographic disruption. Modeled as an exogenous shock process punctuating the trajectory.

constructs.name: cyp2c19_metabolizer_status
constructs.description: CYP2C19 enzyme metabolizer phenotype derived from the rs4244285 genotype call in the 23andMe raw export. Five-level ordinal phenotype (poor → intermediate → normal → rapid → ultrarapid) that scales escitalopram clearance: lower enzyme activity → higher plasma exposure per dose. Time-invariant and directly observed via genotype, so this construct enters the SSM as an exogenous covariate on serotonergic_exposure rather than a marginalized confounder.

constructs.name: baseline_extraversion
constructs.description: Stable trait sociability / extraversion. Shifts baseline social-initiation rate, network breadth, and positive-affect/reward sensitivity, but passive communication traces entangle this trait with current mood, partner availability, work demands, and relationship context. Not directly measured by a validated personality instrument.

edges.description: Pharmacy fill events drive plasma escitalopram concentration with first-order pharmacokinetics (half-life ~32 h in this patient given CYP2C19 *1/*2 intermediate metabolizer status). Steady state achieved within 5-7 days of each dose change.

sources.title: Rao N. (2007). The clinical pharmacokinetics of escitalopram. Clinical Pharmacokinetics, 46(4), 281-290.
sources.snippet: Escitalopram has a mean terminal elimination half-life of ~27-32 h, linear pharmacokinetics across the 10-30 mg dose range, and reaches steady state in ~7-10 days.

edges.description: The initial medication start and the 2024-03-05 dose increase are partly responses to lagged depressive severity and incomplete remission documented at clinical follow-up, so prescribing is not purely exogenous.

sources.title: Trivedi MH, Rush AJ, Wisniewski SR, et al. (2006). Evaluation of outcomes with citalopram for depression using measurement-based care in STAR*D: implications for clinical practice. American Journal of Psychiatry, 163(1), 28-40.
sources.snippet: Measurement-based care drove protocolized dose escalations conditional on lagged symptom severity (QIDS-SR), making antidepressant dose a function of prior outcome rather than an exogenous assignment.

edges.description: Daily pill-taking determines whether each prescribed dose actually contributes to circulating drug. Missed doses produce trough concentrations; ~93% PDC sustains therapeutic plasma levels.

sources.title: Sansone RA, Sansone LA. (2012). Antidepressant adherence: are patients taking their medications? Innovations in Clinical Neuroscience, 9(5-6), 41-46.
sources.snippet: Roughly half of antidepressant patients discontinue or miss doses within the first months; intermittent dosing produces subtherapeutic plasma exposure and is a major modifier of effective drug delivery.

edges.description: 5-HT reuptake inhibition increases synaptic serotonin acutely; downstream neuroadaptive changes (BDNF upregulation, hippocampal neurogenesis, HPA axis recalibration) lift mood with onset typically at week 3-4 and full response by week 8-12.

sources.title: Cipriani A, Furukawa TA, Salanti G, et al. (2018). Comparative efficacy and acceptability of 21 antidepressant drugs for the acute treatment of adults with major depressive disorder: a systematic review and network meta-analysis. The Lancet, 391(10128), 1357-1366.
sources.snippet: Escitalopram showed an SMD of about -0.32 vs. placebo across 522 trials (network meta-analysis), with response onset typically emerging from week 2-4.

sources.title: Duman RS, Aghajanian GK, Sanacora G, Krystal JH. (2016). Synaptic plasticity and depression: new insights from stress and rapid-acting antidepressants. Nature Medicine, 22(3), 238-249.
sources.snippet: SSRI antidepressant action requires weeks of downstream neuroplastic adaptation (BDNF/TrkB signaling, synaptogenesis) rather than acute monoaminergic effects alone, consistent with a 3-8 week therapeutic latency.

edges.description: Restoration of energy and goal-directed motivation as treatment takes effect; activation is a documented behavioral signature of SSRI response.

sources.title: Demyttenaere K, Jaspers L. (2008). Review: bupropion and SSRI-induced side effects. Journal of Psychopharmacology, 22(7), 792-804.
sources.snippet: SSRIs commonly produce a transient activation/agitation profile in early weeks alongside later restoration of psychomotor drive, both of which translate into measurable movement and activity changes.

edges.description: REM suppression (~10-15% of total REM time) is a robust SSRI pharmacological signature; total sleep continuity initially worsens during the first 2-3 weeks of titration (initial-insomnia bump) and improves thereafter as mood stabilizes.

sources.title: Wichniak A, Wierzbicka A, Walęcka M, Jernajczyk W. (2017). Effects of antidepressants on sleep. Current Psychiatry Reports, 19(9), 63.
sources.snippet: SSRIs robustly suppress REM sleep and lengthen REM latency; subjective sleep often worsens transiently during titration and improves with sustained response.

edges.description: Exercise produces independent antidepressant effects via BDNF release, beta-endorphin, behavioral activation, and improved sleep pressure regulation.

sources.title: Schuch FB, Vancampfort D, Richards J, Rosenbaum S, Ward PB, Stubbs B. (2016). Exercise as a treatment for depression: a meta-analysis adjusting for publication bias. Journal of Psychiatric Research, 77, 42-51.
sources.snippet: Adjusted pooled SMD ≈ -1.1 for exercise vs. control on depressive symptoms across 25 RCTs; effect persists after adjusting for publication bias.

edges.description: Sleep deprivation and architectural disruption acutely worsen mood and emotional regulation; restorative sleep produces same-day and next-day improvement.

sources.title: Baglioni C, Battagliese G, Feige B, et al. (2011). Insomnia as a predictor of depression: a meta-analytic evaluation of longitudinal epidemiological studies. Journal of Affective Disorders, 135(1-3), 10-19.
sources.snippet: Non-depressed individuals with insomnia had a ~2.6-fold elevated risk of developing depression (OR ≈ 2.60, 95% CI 1.98-3.42) across 21 longitudinal epidemiological studies.

edges.description: Behavioral activation through social contact directly improves affect; reduced engagement deepens depressive cognition through anhedonia and rumination.

sources.title: Cuijpers P, van Straten A, Warmerdam L. (2007). Behavioral activation treatments of depression: a meta-analysis. Clinical Psychology Review, 27(3), 318-326.
sources.snippet: Behavioral activation, which centers on increasing positively-reinforced (often social) activity, showed a large effect size (d ≈ 0.87) for depression across 16 controlled trials.

sources.title: Santini ZI, Koyanagi A, Tyrovolas S, Mason C, Haro JM. (2015). The association between social relationships and depression: a systematic review. Journal of Affective Disorders, 175, 53-65.
sources.snippet: Perceived social support and contact frequency are consistently inversely associated with depressive symptoms in longitudinal cohorts.

edges.description: Low mood reduces motivation, energy, and goal-directed behavior. Psychomotor retardation lowers spontaneous movement; fatigue lowers exercise initiation.

sources.title: Buyukdura JS, McClintock SM, Croarkin PE. (2011). Psychomotor retardation in depression: biological underpinnings, measurement, and treatment. Progress in Neuro-Psychopharmacology & Biological Psychiatry, 35(2), 395-409.
sources.snippet: Psychomotor retardation is a core feature of melancholic depression and produces objectively measurable reductions in spontaneous movement and gait speed.

edges.description: Depression disrupts sleep continuity and architecture: early-morning awakening, reduced slow-wave sleep, disinhibited REM, or hypersomnia depending on subtype.

sources.title: Nutt D, Wilson S, Paterson L. (2008). Sleep disorders as core symptoms of depression. Dialogues in Clinical Neuroscience, 10(3), 329-336.
sources.snippet: Sleep disturbance (insomnia or hypersomnia) is reported by ~90% of depressed patients; polysomnography typically shows reduced SWS, shortened REM latency, and increased REM density.

edges.description: Depression produces social withdrawal: reduced communication initiation, longer response latencies, narrower partner network, declining shared meals and visits.

sources.title: Kupferberg A, Bicks L, Hasler G. (2016). Social functioning in major depressive disorder. Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews, 69, 313-332.
sources.snippet: MDD is consistently associated with reduced social network size, lower partner-interaction rates, and impaired reward sensitivity to social stimuli.

edges.description: Depressive cognition reduces medication-taking via diminished future-orientation, hopelessness about treatment effectiveness, motor inertia, and disrupted routines.

sources.title: DiMatteo MR, Lepper HS, Croghan TW. (2000). Depression is a risk factor for noncompliance with medical treatment: meta-analysis of the effects of anxiety and depression on patient adherence. Archives of Internal Medicine, 160(14), 2101-2107.
sources.snippet: Across 12 studies, depressed patients had 3x the odds of being non-adherent to medical treatment compared with non-depressed patients (OR ~3.0).

edges.description: Reduced photoperiod (winter at 40.7°N latitude) shifts mood baseline downward through the SAD spectrum: serotonin pathway downregulation and circadian phase delay.

sources.title: Rosenthal NE, Sack DA, Gillin JC, et al. (1984). Seasonal affective disorder: a description of the syndrome and preliminary findings with light therapy. Archives of General Psychiatry, 41(1), 72-80.
sources.snippet: Initial clinical description of recurrent fall/winter depression remitting with bright light, establishing photoperiod as a causal driver of affective state at mid-latitudes.

sources.title: Lam RW, Tam EM. (2009). A Clinician's Guide to Using Light Therapy. Cambridge University Press.
sources.snippet: Subclinical seasonal mood variation is detectable in roughly 10-15% of mid-latitude populations and is driven by photoperiodic regulation of serotonergic and circadian systems.

edges.description: Acute psychosocial stressors (bereavement, relationship loss, family illness) directly worsen mood through HPA-axis activation and cognitive appraisal pathways.

sources.title: Kendler KS, Karkowski LM, Prescott CA. (1999). Causal relationship between stressful life events and the onset of major depression. American Journal of Psychiatry, 156(6), 837-841.
sources.snippet: In a co-twin control design, the odds ratio for MDD onset in the month of a stressful life event was 5.64 overall and remained 3.58 within monozygotic pairs, supporting a substantially causal stressor → depression effect not fully explained by shared genetic liability.

edges.description: Major life changes alter the structure and accessibility of the social network: a breakup removes the primary partner, a move alters peer proximity, family illness redirects social attention.

sources.title: Holmes TH, Rahe RH. (1967). The Social Readjustment Rating Scale. Journal of Psychosomatic Research, 11(2), 213-218.
sources.snippet: Foundational instrument quantifying readjustment demand of major life events (bereavement, divorce, relocation, illness); each event is defined in part by its direct disruption of social-role structure.

edges.description: CYP2C19 enzyme activity scales escitalopram first-order clearance (~32 h half-life at *1/*2 intermediate metabolizer status; faster at *1/*1, slower at *2/*2). The phenotype shifts plasma exposure per dose without affecting affective_state directly.

sources.title: Hicks JK, Bishop JR, Sangkuhl K, et al. (2015). Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium (CPIC) guideline for CYP2D6 and CYP2C19 genotypes and dosing of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors. Clinical Pharmacology & Therapeutics, 98(2), 127-134.
sources.snippet: CPIC guideline recommends 50% starting-dose reduction for CYP2C19 poor metabolizers on escitalopram; intermediate metabolizers (*1/*2) show modestly elevated plasma exposure per mg dose.

edges.description: Trait sociability shifts the person-specific baseline rate of social initiation, partner-network breadth, and shared-activity frequency, while day-to-day deviations remain partly driven by mood and context.

sources.title: Asendorpf JB, Wilpers S. (1998). Personality effects on social relationships. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 74(6), 1531-1544.
sources.snippet: Extraversion prospectively predicted number and contact frequency of peer relationships across an 18-month longitudinal study of young adults.

edges.description: Trait extraversion may contribute to baseline positive affectivity, reward sensitivity, and stress buffering. The edge represents a broad trait prior rather than a decisive predictor of this patient's depressive trajectory.

sources.title: Kotov R, Gamez W, Schmidt F, Watson D. (2010). Linking 'big' personality traits to anxiety, depressive, and substance use disorders: a meta-analysis. Psychological Bulletin, 136(5), 768-821.
sources.snippet: Low extraversion was modestly but consistently associated with MDD (r ≈ -0.25 across 175 studies), supporting a stable trait-level contribution to depression vulnerability; effect was larger for dysthymia and social phobia.

messages.content: You are a clinical psychiatrist specializing in mood-disorder pharmacotherapy and N-of-1 causal inference. Your task is to propose a latent causal model for a patient's individual-level question about antidepressant efficacy. Identify theoretical constructs (latent variables), causal edges between them, the outcome construct, and the treatment construct(s). Constraints: (1) outcome must be endogenous and have ≥1 incoming edge; (2) directed contemporaneous edges between two endogenous time-varying constructs are forbidden — represent feedback as lagged; (3) exogenous constructs cannot be effects; (4) time-varying constructs cannot cause time-invariant ones. After drafting the model, call validate_latent_model with the JSON to verify constraints.

Patient question (verbatim): "I've been on escitalopram for about two and a half years. I'm thinking about tapering. Has the medication actually been moving the needle, or did I just get better on my own — and what would my likely trajectory look like if I taper now versus continue another six months?"

Patient profile from records summary: 38 y/o F software engineer, single MDD episode Aug-Nov 2023 precipitated by relationship loss and work stressor, started escitalopram 10mg 11/17/2023, escalated to 20mg 03/05/2024, sustained remission since (one stress-test episode around mother's cancer diagnosis 10/2025 with intact functioning). Available data: pharmacy fill history (CVS DSAR, 15 fills), GP visit notes (Cobble Hill Family Practice, 5 encounters with PHQ-9 trajectory 16→13→8→4→3), Day One journal (~20 entries), Apple Health export.xml (steps/exercise/walking speed/State of Mind from iOS 17.3+, 2022-2026), Oura ring sleep + readiness JSON v2 (1448 nights), iMessage volume + excerpt threads (Jess best friend, Mom, deceased father ritual thread, ex-partner frozen, current partner, book club, brother), Google Calendar ICS (~50 events including therapy/climbing/pottery RRULEs and CANCELLED markers during episode), Plaid via Monarch (~50 transactions including therapy + Rx copays, takeout spike during episode), 23andMe raw (CYP2C19 *1/*2 from rs4244285 AG = intermediate metabolizer; BDNF Val/Val; MTHFR C677T het; FKBP5 het).

Propose the latent causal model. Use validate_latent_model to verify before responding.

I'll propose 11 constructs and 19 causal edges grounded in SSRI pharmacology, depressive-episode dynamics, symptom-responsive prescribing, and behavioral mediation.

Constructs:
1. **affective_state** (endogenous, time-varying, OUTCOME) — composite over mood/anhedonia/energy/concentration.
2. **serotonergic_exposure** (endogenous, time-varying) — effective escitalopram exposure, governed by fills, adherence, and patient-specific pharmacokinetic priors.
3. **adherence** (endogenous, time-varying) — daily pill-taking, with depressive cognition reducing adherence.
4-6. **sleep_quality, physical_activity, social_engagement** — mediator/reverse-causation triad.
7. **prescription_event** (endogenous, time-varying) — clinician-mediated prescribing/fill events. The initial start and 2024-03-05 dose increase are partly responses to lagged symptoms, so prescribing cannot be treated as purely exogenous.
8-9. **seasonal_load, life_events_load** (exogenous, time-varying) — photoperiod and acute external stressors.
10. **cyp2c19_metabolizer_status** (exogenous, time-invariant, OBSERVED) — directly read from the 23andMe rs4244285 genotype call; 5-level ordinal phenotype that scales escitalopram clearance per dose. Edges into serotonergic_exposure as an exogenous PK covariate.
11. **baseline_extraversion** (exogenous, time-invariant, latent) — stable sociability/reward-sensitivity trait. Dual outgoing structure (social_engagement + affective_state) creates a real backdoor for the social_engagement treatment effect. Passive communication traces are informative but not a validated trait measure.

Two trait constructs were considered and rejected on the principle that a time-invariant unmeasured trait only earns inclusion in the DAG when it has multiple outgoing edges that form an unblockable backdoor for some treatment. (a) A broad polygenic depression vulnerability with only a single edge into affective_state would be absorbed into the person-specific intercept for an N-of-1 question and contributes nothing to within-person identification. (b) baseline_chronotype was likewise dropped to keep the DAG minimal: a single retained latent confounder (extraversion) is enough to demonstrate the framework's non-identification handling for a behavioral treatment.

Edges: (a) treatment chain prescription_event -> serotonergic_exposure <- adherence; serotonergic_exposure -> affective_state. (b) Behavioral mediation: serotonergic_exposure -> {physical_activity, sleep_quality} -> affective_state, plus social_engagement -> affective_state. (c) Reverse causation, all lagged: affective_state -> {physical_activity, sleep_quality, social_engagement, adherence, prescription_event}. (d) Exogenous drivers: seasonal_load -> affective_state; life_events_load -> {affective_state, social_engagement}. (e) Time-invariant inputs: cyp2c19_metabolizer_status -> serotonergic_exposure (observed PK covariate); baseline_extraversion -> {social_engagement, affective_state}.

Stage 1b should preserve the medication question as a total treatment-regimen estimand: passive observational data cannot separate pharmacology from expectation/placebo. Social_engagement remains the lone non-identifiable treatment because its trait confounder (extraversion) is not directly measured. Sleep_quality is now identifiable via temporal adjustment alone. Marginalizing the single latent time-invariant trait (extraversion) should induce one initial-state correlation; cyp2c19_metabolizer_status is observed and does not marginalize.
messages.reasoning:
The patient is asking a within-person causal question with symptom-responsive treatment history. That means the medication exposure is not randomized: the initial prescription followed a moderate-severe episode, and the March 2024 dose increase followed partial response rather than remission. The DAG therefore keeps prescription_event endogenous and adds a lagged affective_state -> prescription_event edge, while allowing lagged affective_state adjustment to carry the within-person identification argument for serotonergic_exposure.

Key modeling decisions: (1) Prescription_event is not purely exogenous. Fills still drive subsequent exposure, but prescribing decisions respond to lagged symptoms and clinician follow-up. (2) Pharmacogenetic background is included only where it does causal work: cyp2c19_metabolizer_status is directly observed via the 23andMe rs4244285 genotype call and enters the DAG as an exogenous time-invariant covariate on serotonergic_exposure (PK scaling). (3) A trait-level construct earns its place in the DAG only if it has multiple outgoing edges forming an unblockable backdoor for some treatment. baseline_extraversion qualifies because extraversion -> {social_engagement, affective_state} blocks identification of the social_engagement treatment effect, and that non-identification beat is exactly what the framework needs to demonstrate honestly. Polygenic depression vulnerability and chronotype were considered and rejected: a single-outgoing-edge unmeasured trait into affective_state is absorbed into the person-specific intercept for N-of-1 and contributes nothing to within-person identification, while keeping a second backdoor confounder (chronotype) is redundant once one already demonstrates the non-identification path. (4) Because the surviving latent trait is time-invariant, its marginalization belongs in initial-state covariance structure rather than process innovation covariance.

Expected Stage 1b verdict: serotonergic_exposure, physical_activity, sleep_quality, and adherence are estimable treatment effects after temporal adjustment; social_engagement is withheld from point estimates and reported as a structural sensitivity question. One initial_state_correlation induced dependency (extraversion) should appear in the EstimationSpec.

messages.content: Latent model validated. Outcome: affective_state. Treatments to evaluate at Stage 1b: serotonergic_exposure (the primary clinical question), sleep_quality, physical_activity, social_engagement, adherence. Prescription_event is modeled as endogenous because medication initiation and dose escalation are partly symptom-responsive. Anticipated Stage 1b filtering: social_engagement flagged non-identifiable under conservative extraversion handling; the remaining four should clear identification via temporal adjustment. The single retained time-invariant trait confounder should induce one initial-state correlation after marginalization.
